evidence_items.explanation: The study assessed 517 programming answers and reported 52% incorrect, demonstrating mixed accuracy. Its 12-participant user study found that plausible presentation could obscure errors, directly supporting the user-detection component.

The January report documents frequent factual errors in legal queries and unreliable model self-assessment. It supports the absence of a dependable confidence signal, although it does not directly measure end-user detection.

unresolved_gaps: The studies do not provide a population-wide error-detection rate for ordinary users across all domains.
The legal report's event date identifies the January 2024 reported state; an exact experimental collection date was not established.
